findings.label: Lobular membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis
findings.evidence: Type II membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis characterized by mesangial matrix and cellular increases is responsible for a lobular accentuation

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (a, b, c). a: PAS light microscopy of a human renal biopsy in a dense deposit disease case (article title and in-text dense-deposit biopsy); the caption explicitly describes an MPGN type II pattern with lobular accentuation, the classic membranoproliferative pattern of DDD. Pediatric eGFR by the 2009 Schwartz formula in the text indicates a child patient. b: High-power PAS of the same DDD renal biopsy; the caption states the intense peripheral basement membrane staining represents dense deposit material, the pathognomonic intramembranous dense deposits of DDD. c: Direct immunofluorescence of the same human DDD biopsy showing segmental pseudolinear/granular IgM along the capillary wall. Disease attribution to DDD rests on the disease-focused article title and the captioned biopsy, but the deposited immunoglobulin is IgM rather than the classic C3-dominant DDD staining, so the C3 vocabulary key is not applied and the finding is recorded as proposed.
panels.attribution_text: Berthe-Aucejo et al. Blockade of alternative complement pathway in dense deposit disease.. Case reports in nephrology 2014. doi:10.1155/2014/201568. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: (a) Type II membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis characterized by mesangial matrix and cellular increases is responsible for a lobular accentuation associated with a diffuse and intense staining of the peripheral basement membrane (periodic acid-Schiff [PAS], magnification [G]: ×200). (b) The diffuse and intense staining of the peripheral basement membrane indicates the presence of dense deposit material (PAS, G ×2000). (c) Immunofluorescence techniques show segmental pseudo linear and granular IgM deposits along the peripheral capillary wall (fluorescein isothiocyanate anti-IgM, G ×100).
in_text_mentions: /L, and eGFR was 93 mL/min/1.73/m² according to the 2009 Schwartz formula. A second renal biopsy was realized and showed dense deposits in 100% of glomerulus and 15% of interstitial fibrosis (Figures 1(a), 1(b), and 1(c)). The patient was vaccinated with Menactra to prevent Neisseria meningitidis infection as a preparation prior to introduce eculizumab. Initial schedule was similar to those proposed in patients with atypical haemolytic uremic syndrome, namely, 900 mg every week for 4 weeks and then 1200 mg on week 5 and every 2 weeks. Treatment was associated with penicillin V treatment. After

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Human renal biopsy light microscopy (PAM) showing segmental GBM double contour and focal endocapillary proliferation, glomerular manifestations directly attributed to dense deposit disease in this case report. b: Human renal biopsy PAS stain showing massive diffuse interstitial inflammatory cell infiltration, part of the renal pathology in this dense deposit disease case with associated tubulointerstitial nephritis; no vocabulary key covers interstitial nephritis, so recorded as a proposed finding. c: Human renal biopsy immunofluorescence showing weak (1+) IgG on capillary walls and mesangium, part of the same dense deposit disease biopsy; the weak IgG is a minor accompanying stain, not the C3-dominant pattern. d: Human renal biopsy immunofluorescence showing strong (2+) C3 staining on capillary walls and mesangium with a garland pattern, the classic C3-dominant glomerular staining of dense deposit disease.

A few eosinophilic cells were seen (b). Immunofluorescence analysis revealed 1 + positive results for IgG (c) and 2 + positive results for C3 on the capillary walls and mesangium area (d).
